data.title: Zaggle Prepaid Ocean Services' (NSE:ZAGGLE) Shareholders May Want To Dig Deeper Than Statutory Profit
data.description:
The market shrugged off Zaggle Prepaid Ocean Services Limited's (NSE:ZAGGLE) solid earnings report. Our analysis showed that there are some concerning factors in the earnings that investors may be cautious of.

AI is about to change healthcare. These 20 stocks are working on everything from early diagnostics to drug discovery. The best part - they are all under $10bn in marketcap - there is still time to get in early.

Examining Cashflow Against Zaggle Prepaid Ocean Services' Earnings

In high finance, the key ratio used to measure how well a company converts reported profits into free cash flow (FCF) is the accrual ratio (from cashflow). To get the accrual ratio we first subtract FCF from profit for a period, and then divide that number by the average operating assets for the period. The ratio shows us how much a company's profit exceeds its FCF.

As a result, a negative accrual ratio is a positive for the company, and a positive accrual ratio is a negative. That is not intended to imply we should worry about a positive accrual ratio, but it's worth noting where the accrual ratio is rather high. That's because some academic studies have suggested that high accruals ratios tend to lead to lower profit or less profit growth.

Over the twelve months to September 2026, Zaggle Prepaid Ocean Services recorded an accrual ratio of 0.32. Therefore, we know that it's free cashflow was significantly lower than its statutory profit, raising questions about how useful that profit figure really is. Even though it reported a profit of ₹1.19b, a look at free cash flow indicates it actually burnt through ₹1.7b in the last year. We also note that Zaggle Prepaid Ocean Services' free cash flow was actually negative last year as well, so we could understand if shareholders were bothered by its outflow of ₹1.7b.

data.title: There May Be Underlying Issues With The Quality Of GAON CABLE's (KRX:000500) Earnings
data.description:
GAON CABLE Co., Ltd. (KRX:000500) announced strong profits, but the stock was stagnant. Our analysis suggests that this might be because shareholders have noticed some concerning underlying factors.

This technology could replace computers: discover the 20 stocks are working to make quantum computing a reality.

Examining Cashflow Against GAON CABLE's Earnings

One key financial ratio used to measure how well a company converts its profit to free cash flow (FCF) is the accrual ratio. The accrual ratio subtracts the FCF from the profit for a given period, and divides the result by the average operating assets of the company over that time. The ratio shows us how much a company's profit exceeds its FCF.

As a result, a negative accrual ratio is a positive for the company, and a positive accrual ratio is a negative. While it's not a problem to have a positive accrual ratio, indicating a certain level of non-cash profits, a high accrual ratio is arguably a bad thing, because it indicates paper profits are not matched by cash flow. To quote a 2014 paper by Lewellen and Resutek, "firms with higher accruals tend to be less profitable in the future".

GAON CABLE has an accrual ratio of 0.32 for the year to September 2026. Therefore, we know that it's free cashflow was significantly lower than its statutory profit, raising questions about how useful that profit figure really is. In the last twelve months it actually had negative free cash flow, with an outflow of ₩194b despite its profit of ₩75.6b, mentioned above. We saw that FCF was ₩48b a year ago though, so GAON CABLE has at least been able to generate positive FCF in the past.

What The Results Changed For The SES AI Thesis

The most concrete news was that SES AI reaffirmed its 2026 revenue guidance of US$30 million to US$35 million and signed multiyear ESS and drone related contracts, which supported the bullish focus on multiple business lines. At the same time, class action filings over alleged revenue misstatements and Q3 2026 figures showing revenue down while the loss narrowed, with net margin still at -201.6%, kept the profitability part of the optimistic case unproven. Overall, the evidence cut both ways.

The key lesson is about what to test first. When a story hangs on rapid revenue compounding and a fast swing to double digit margins, you can track that by watching reported top line, net income and net margin each quarter against the original growth and profitability assumptions that justified the Fair Value range.

SES AI Today, And What The Price Really Reflects

Today SES AI trades at US$0.36, with the story now anchored less to hype and more to whether operations can climb out of heavy losses. Revenue in Q3 2026 was US$6.64 million compared with US$7.118 million a year earlier, while the loss narrowed and net margin improved from very deep negative territory to -201.6%.
